brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Level 0 has three full hex bases (0,0,0), (1,0,0) and a stack base (0,0,1) on level 1; level 1 holds a two-compartment bin (bin:0,0,1). The tower is two storeys tall (measured via the configurator, check_build clean, meshClash clear).

Two notch drawers on level 0: notch:0#0,1 (drawer frame, female-male hand) at cell (0,1,0) and notch:0#1,-1 (drawer frame, male-female hand) at cell (1,-1,0). The BOM lists two Notch drawer bodies with runners and lids.

The tower is a freestanding block of hex bases with caps closing the open faces and joints bolted (lockJoints). The configurator has no bench-mounting or clamping feature, so how it is fixed to a bench is not modelled and was not checked.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey hex-base storage tower: three full bases (two on the ground storey, one stacked on top at (0,0,1)), two notch drawers on the ground storey, a two-compartment bin on the upper storey, open faces capped and joints bolted. check_build reports no issues and meshClash is clear. Material suitability (PETG, load on drawers) is not checked by the configurator; the bolt torque note in the BOM says to hand-tighten M6 bolts to about 2 N.m.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
